blocks.text: November 24th, 1971. The day before Thanksgiving. A man in a dark suit buys a ticket from Portland to Seattle. Twenty dollars, cash. The name he gives: Dan Cooper.
In the air, he hands the flight attendant a note. I have a bomb in my briefcase. I want you to sit next to me.
His demands are simple. Two hundred thousand dollars in twenty-dollar bills. And four parachutes.
In Seattle, he gets both. He lets all thirty-six passengers go. Then he orders the crew to take off again, heading for Mexico. Fly low, he says. Fly slow.
Around eight o'clock that night, somewhere over the forests of Washington State, in the dark, in a storm, he lowers the stairs at the back of the plane. And jumps.
He is never seen again. No body. No parachute. The FBI looks at more than eight hundred suspects.

Nine years later, an eight-year-old boy digging on a riverbank finds bundles of rotting twenty-dollar bills. Five thousand eight hundred dollars. The serial numbers match. The rest of the money has never turned up.
In 2016, the FBI closed the case. Unsolved. Nobody knows who he was. Or whether he survived the fall.
